rows.label: Babe Ruth
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Sultan of Swat and became baseball's first true superstar slugger

rows.label: Shohei Ohtani
rows.hook: stars as both a power-hitting slugger and an ace pitcher, a feat almost nobody manages

rows.label: Aaron Judge
rows.hook: smashed 62 home runs in a single season to set the American League record

rows.label: Rickey Henderson
rows.description: American Hall of Fame baseball player (1958–2024)
rows.hook: stole more bases than anyone else in major league history

rows.label: Don Mattingly
rows.hook: was a beloved first baseman and captain who never won a World Series ring as a player

rows.label: Joe DiMaggio
rows.hook: put together a 56-game hitting streak that has never been matched

rows.label: Lou Gehrig
rows.hook: was called the Iron Horse before a disease that now carries his name ended his career

rows.label: Mickey Mantle
rows.hook: was a switch-hitting center fielder famous for tape-measure home runs

rows.label: Mike Trout
rows.hook: is a center fielder widely called the best all-around player of his generation

rows.label: Barry Bonds
rows.hook: holds the all-time career home run record, a mark that sparked years of controversy

rows.label: Pete Rose
rows.hook: holds the record for most career hits but was banned from the sport for gambling

rows.label: Carl Yastrzemski
rows.hook: was the last hitter to win the batting Triple Crown before Miguel Cabrera did it

rows.label: Ichiro Suzuki
rows.hook: set the single-season hits record after starring in Japan before coming to America

rows.label: Albert Pujols
rows.hook: became one of only a handful of sluggers to reach 700 career home runs

rows.label: Ken Griffey Jr.
rows.hook: was a sweet-swinging center fielder who famously wore his cap backward

rows.label: Ted Williams
rows.description: American baseball player and fighter pilot
rows.hook: was the last major leaguer to hit .400 in a season

rows.label: Yogi Berra
rows.description: American baseball player, manager, and coach (1925–2015)
rows.hook: was a catcher whose mangled-sounding sayings are as famous as his ten championship rings

rows.label: Sandy Koufax
rows.hook: was a dominant lefty who retired at the top of his game because of a sore elbow

rows.label: Cal Ripken Jr.
rows.hook: broke baseball's famous consecutive-games record, earning the nickname Iron Man

rows.label: Ty Cobb
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Georgia Peach and owns the highest career batting average ever

rows.label: Tony Gwynn
rows.description: American Hall of Fame baseball right fielder; 1960-2014
rows.hook: won eight batting titles with a famously sweet left-handed swing

rows.label: Mike Piazza
rows.hook: went from a 62nd-round afterthought pick to the greatest-hitting catcher in history

rows.label: Clayton Kershaw
rows.hook: is a lefty ace with a devastating curveball and multiple Cy Young Awards

rows.label: Mariano Rivera
rows.description: Panamanian Hall of Fame baseball player, relief pitcher
rows.hook: retired as the all-time saves leader while throwing mostly one pitch, the cutter

rows.label: David Ortiz
rows.hook: was nicknamed Big Papi and delivered countless clutch hits in October

rows.label: Sammy Sosa
rows.hook: chased the single-season home run record in a famous duel with Mark McGwire

rows.label: Hank Aaron
rows.hook: broke Babe Ruth's career home run record and held it for over thirty years

rows.label: Honus Wagner
rows.hook: is pictured on the T206 baseball card, one of the most valuable ever sold

rows.label: Stan Musial
rows.hook: was known simply as The Man and collected more than 3,000 hits with a corkscrew stance

rows.label: Tom Seaver
rows.hook: was nicknamed The Franchise and won three Cy Young Awards

rows.label: Johnny Bench
rows.hook: is widely considered the greatest catcher ever and starred on the Big Red Machine

rows.label: Ernie Banks
rows.hook: was a cheerful slugging shortstop famous for saying Let's play two

rows.label: Bob Gibson
rows.hook: posted one of the lowest earned run averages ever in the so-called Year of the Pitcher

rows.label: Walter Johnson
rows.description: American Hall of Fame baseball player (1887-1946)
rows.hook: was a fastball pitcher nicknamed The Big Train who won 417 games
